risks.risk: PLANNER-FOUND GAP: the objective assumed the app could measure which keys vary across series, but `metadata.py:688` ships only `images[0].keys` to the UI (`key_paths`). Without plumbing, B-2's discrimination axis would have been silently computed over one image, quietly classifying all 95 keys as 'constant' (or all as 'varying') and making the Suggested tier meaningless — while every test still passed.
risks.mitigation: T5 adds `image_key_paths` (per-image raw key dicts) through the worker payload -> ExtractionDetail -> SuggestionResult, leaving `key_paths` byte-identical so no existing consumer changes; T9's ranker takes the per-image list and T11 falls back to `[key_paths]` when it is empty. T5 is in batch 0 so both consumers can depend on it.

risks.risk: PLANNER-FOUND SCOPE CORRECTION: A-1's policy reversal is stated in five places in llm.py, not the two the objective named (module docstring, function docstring, hard rule 3, hard rule 8, and the contradicting 'authoritative context' line). Editing only rules 7-8 would leave the prompt and the public docstrings still asserting the opposite policy — the exact self-contradiction the C1 verifier already flagged.
risks.mitigation: T3's scope enumerates all five locations as a single coherent edit and its verification greps for the absence of the two old policy strings plus the survival of the no-fabrication rule.

risks.risk: A unit-anchored magnification regex `(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*[xX]\b` alone would REGRESS the most common real input: LIF's atomic `Magnification` key value is the bare string '40' (and OME's `NominalMagnification` is '63'), neither of which contains an 'x'. A naive B-0 fix returns None there and silently drops magnification from every LIF filename.
risks.mitigation: T1 mandates a two-stage parse (unit-anchored first, then a whole-string bare-number fallback, never 'first number anywhere') and its verification asserts the exact 7-value output vector including '40'->'X40' and '63'->'X63'.

risks.risk: B-1's family matching could promote an atomic-looking but wrong key ahead of a curated one — e.g. `ChannelName='Green'` (atomic, 5 chars) jumping ahead of `Dyes` and resurrecting the GREEN-BLUE-RED colour-name bug (repo invariant E2), or a stem collapse pulling an unrelated key into a field's family.
risks.mitigation: T6 confines family-discovered keys to a strict tier 1 that can never reorder the existing exact-key tier 0, applies the atomic-first sort within tier 1 only, and adds an explicit guard test that an image with both `Dyes` and `ChannelName='Green'` still resolves markers from `Dyes`. Verification also runs `-m integration` since resolve_fields feeds format-routed extraction whose coverage is deselected by default (lesson 34 / E4).

risks.risk: The AppTest harness is the load-bearing assumption for five tasks, and `at.data_editor` does not exist in streamlit 1.60 — a naive smoke test would try to read the Tag Files editor, fail to find it, and be 'fixed' by asserting something weaker that proves nothing (e.g. only that no exception was raised).
risks.mitigation: The planner already booted the real app under AppTest and confirmed zero exceptions, button-by-label access and `at.dataframe`; every smoke task's scope states that assertions go against `at.session_state['suggestions']`, that dataframes are identified by content not index, and T2 is instructed to report a BLOCKING discovery rather than substitute an alternative approach if the harness cannot drive the app.

risks.risk: A smoke test could leave real artifacts in the repo: the app creates `naming_scheme.json` in the CWD at startup and the mapping test writes a profile, so a test run from the repo root would dirty the working tree and could overwrite the user's real config or profile.
risks.mitigation: `boot_app` must `monkeypatch.chdir(tmp_path)` (verified working — the spike created naming_scheme.json inside the temp dir), all profiles are written under tmp_path, and T2/T11 verification includes `git status --porcelain` checks on naming_scheme.json and profiles/.

risks.risk: The proposal-review UI could apply an override through a path other than an explicit accept (a rerun, or the 'Apply tags & preview names' handler picking up the proposed value), turning a reviewable proposal back into the silent overwrite A-1 exists to prevent.
risks.mitigation: T10 stores proposals in session_state only, never in `s.fields`, and its smoke test (b) asserts that without an accept the value and source stay at their metadata-derived originals; accepted overrides are tagged `llm_description` so they still read as provisional through Tag Files, Planned Renames and the pre-Apply block.

risks.risk: Streamlit's `st.cache_data` on `_cached_ollama_models` is process-global with a 60s TTL, so one smoke test's stubbed model list can leak into the next and make the A-2 'Ollama unreachable' test pass or fail for the wrong reason.
risks.mitigation: `boot_app` clears `st.cache_data` before every run, and T8's verification requires demonstrating that the non-invocation test FAILS when the gate is removed and PASSES when restored — falsifying the alternative rather than confirming the happy path.

risks.risk: Three tasks (T8, T10, T11) rewrite overlapping regions of app_streamlit.py, and two (T1, T6) overlap in field_map.py; a later executor could revert an earlier task's edit while reconciling a dirty tree.
risks.mitigation: Batches are ordered so no two tasks touching the same file ever run together (app_streamlit.py: batch 1 -> 2 -> 3; field_map.py: batch 0 -> 1; service.py: batch 0 -> 1), and each dependent task's scope explicitly names the prior edit and says to inspect the diff and build on it rather than revert or re-apply it.
